findings.reason: the followup is the plan's invocation of record, so a section it never names is never built, and without the §5 declaration §9 can land ahead of the change its premise assumes.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` has no `s9` entry and followup `f-arcwc-001` at :94 still orders only §2, §3, §5, §6 and §7, although §9's Why rests on §5's node (`_store._declared_north_stars`, which at `reckon/_store.py:837` still calls `compose_project_state`) and s5 is declared `implementable` rather than done; a coordinator following the followup never dispatches §9, and one dispatching it has no declaration telling it to wait for §5

findings.reason: the mechanism determines whether the zero-compose case and the payload-parity case are simultaneously satisfiable, and leaving it to the node is how one of the two gets quietly dropped.
findings.text: the Deliverable restates the goal ("reads that plan's state and the project-level fields it shows, without composing any other plan") and names no mechanism, where every neighbouring section names the concrete change, while `index_discovery` (`reckon/mcp_views.py:1174`) must still return `sprints`, `milestones`, `blockers`, `timeline`, `active_sprint_id`, `north_stars` and `resource_versions` and `read_plan`'s summary consumes `sprints` through `_plan_blocker_state` (`reckon/mcp.py:1801-1809`); a node must therefore design the cheaper project-level read itself and judge unaided whether its payload can hold equal

findings.reason: either §9 must declare the §5 dependency and its own base, or its done-when must say which plan shape it counts, otherwise the node fails its own gate on code it is not permitted to touch.
findings.text: on main a distributed `read_plan(view="summary")` of a plan that names a north star composes the project a second time through `_store._add_north_star_diagnostic` → `_declared_north_stars` (`reckon/_store.py:736`, `:837`), which §5 removes and which lies outside §9's declared write paths (`reckon/mcp_views.py` and the new test), so §9's "composes no other plan's state" count cannot reach zero in its own fence for such a plan

findings.reason: an unnamed patch target lets the count case pass on the function under test, so the negative control ("restores the whole-project build") would fail the case for the wrong reason or not at all.
findings.text: the first case counts "through a patch on the composer" without naming the function, and the nearest candidate to patch is `_project_state_lists` itself (`reckon/mcp_views.py:1265`), the function the section changes, which would make the count trivially zero without measuring any composition
